notices.summary: Runneth's Inspo creator and organic TikTok guidance ships with the next deploy.
notices.impact: Agent Builder PR #2237 adds Runneth guidance for the next-release Inspo endpoints and teaches Runneth to distinguish direct-queryable routes from broad asks that would otherwise require pulling a batch and inspecting it manually. This is not live until the next deploy.
notices.workaround: Until the next deploy, do not promise the expanded Inspo routes as live. Use currently live data surfaces, or set expectations for what the next release will support: known creator lookup by name or handle, current organic recommendation feed, exact creator feed by handle, saved board examples, competitor ads from unique creatives, and organic keyword update plans with user sign-off.

resolution.label: Next deploy
resolution.note: The Runneth guidance update is in Agent Builder PR #2237 and goes live with the next deploy.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Show under Data access and Inspo. Frame this as next-release creative discovery, not an endpoint outage. The Runneth behavior update and expanded Inspo routing from PR #2237 ship with the next deploy. Make the status card clear about what will be directly queryable versus what would only be a broad batch inspection.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks for creator discovery, creators like a person or brand, top creators in a category, high-engagement creators, organic TikToks about a keyword or topic, organic TikTok search, organic TikTok trends, or changes to organic TikTok feed keywords.
notices.runnethGuidance: PR #2237 injects Runneth to say that organic TikTok and creator discovery are getting richer, but Runneth cannot live-search every TikTok by topic, filter organic TikTok posts by keyword/topic/category/engagement, or filter creators by category, follower range, platform, or engagement from these endpoints yet. After the next deploy, Runneth should offer the strongest direct-queryable path: search a known creator profile by name or handle, inspect the current organic recommendation feed, pull an exact creator feed when the user has a handle, mine saved board examples, use Inspo unique creatives for competitor ad inspiration, or read and update organic TikTok keywords with sign-off to steer future recommendations. If the user still wants a broad creator or organic read, Runneth may pull a current feed or broad batch and inspect it manually, but it should say that this is batch inspection rather than a filtered search and that it may take a while.
notices.supportGuidance: Until the next deploy lands, do not assume Runneth will consistently give this guidance or access these expanded Inspo routes on its own. For broad creator or organic asks, collect the intended strategy angle: target brand, category, creator handle, board, competitor, or keywords. Set expectations that organic keyword changes guide future recommendations and may take time to show new posts, and that broad batch inspection is slower and less precise than direct filtering.

notices.summary: Routine automation is temporarily paused during the refactor.
notices.impact: New scheduled, recurring, monitored, reminder, post-later, or background-upkeep work should not be presented as live reliable automation.
notices.workaround: Save the routine plan with cadence, trigger, task, workspace scope, and delivery target, then do the immediate one-time work where possible.

resolution.label: In progress
resolution.note: Working toward the next planned release as part of the routines refactor; not marked ready yet.

notices.statusPageGuidance: CSMs should treat new routine setup as paused. Save the routine plan and do immediate one-time work where possible.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks to create, set up, schedule, monitor, remind, notify, post later, repeat, keep something updated, or run background upkeep.
notices.runnethGuidance: Lead with the constructive boundary, offer a future routine plan, and avoid saying anything is scheduled until creation actually succeeds.
notices.supportGuidance: Capture cadence, trigger, task, workspace scope, and delivery destination so the plan can be turned on later.

notices.summary: Older Slack installs may need reconnect to use the narrower permission scope.
notices.impact: Some workspaces connected Slack before Runneth's Slack app moved to the narrower permission scope. Those older installs may still show or retain the wider grant until Slack is removed and reconnected through Runneth; newly connected orgs already use the narrower scope.
notices.workaround: Use Runneth's own Slack removal and reconnect flow: ask Runneth to remove Slack, then start a new conversation and ask Runneth to connect Slack again. Do not uninstall the app directly from Slack.

resolution.label: Notice only
resolution.note: Guidance for older installs; no release fix is implied.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Keep Slack as a standalone native OAuth card. This is permission/reconnect guidance for older installs, not a current outage for new Slack connections.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks about Slack permissions, Slack security review, Slack reconnect, Slack reinstall, or replacing an older Slack install with the narrower scope.
notices.runnethGuidance: Explain that new Slack connections already use the narrower scope, while older workspaces may need a Runneth-managed reconnect to pick it up. Route through Runneth's integration removal and reconnect flow. Do not tell customers to uninstall directly from Slack, because that can leave the Runneth web setup widget or reinstall path unable to reconnect cleanly.
notices.supportGuidance: Confirm whether the org is a new install or an older Slack install. If it is older, tell the customer to remove and reconnect Slack through Runneth rather than uninstalling from Slack directly.

notices.impact: Runneth cannot read file uploads on Slack. Web uploads are fine.
notices.workaround: Slack-side retry or new-conversation attempts are unreliable and may only work sometimes. For urgent work, use web upload, paste the text, or describe the file.

resolution.label: Next release
resolution.note: Confirmed for the next planned release.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Show under Slack only. Web uploads are fine. Use the confirmed_next_release resolution flag, but keep the notice active until the release ships.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks to upload, attach, send, read, or analyze a file, screenshot, image, or document in Slack, or reports that a Slack file-upload message got no reply or stalled.
notices.runnethGuidance: Acknowledge that Runneth cannot read file uploads on Slack right now, while web uploads are fine. Starting a new Slack conversation might work sometimes, but it is not dependable and should not be presented as a reliable workaround or fix. For urgent work, ask them to use web upload, paste the relevant text, or describe the file. If the user asks when this is fixed, say the fix is ready and goes out with the next planned release.
notices.supportGuidance: Confirm the upload happened in Slack. Capture whether the Slack conversation was new or an existing thread, the approximate time, file type, and whether the message received no reply, timed out, or failed before sending.

notices.summary: Older Slack threads can show messy formatting.
notices.impact: Replies in older Slack threads may render with messy formatting or raw response-control text instead of a normal Runneth reply.
notices.workaround: Start a new Slack conversation for the same work. If context matters, paste the relevant context or link the older thread in the new conversation.

resolution.label: Next release
resolution.note: Confirmed for the next planned release.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Show under Slack as an active known issue. Show the example thread link for internal context, and use the confirmed_next_release resolution flag, but keep the notice active until the release ships.

examples.label: Example older Slack thread with messy formatting
examples.whatToLookFor: Runneth posts raw response-control JSON in the Slack thread instead of staying silent or sending a normal reply.

notices.runnethTrigger: User asks about or reports messy formatting in an older Slack thread, raw response-control text, or a stale Slack thread that is not rendering Runneth replies normally.
notices.runnethGuidance: Acknowledge that older Slack threads can show messy formatting until the next planned release. Do not proactively mention this for normal Slack requests. For now, starting a new Slack conversation is the cleaner path. If the user needs continuity from the older thread, ask them to paste the relevant context or link the old thread in the new conversation. If the user asks when this is fixed, say the fix is ready and goes out with the next planned release.
notices.supportGuidance: Capture the Slack thread link, whether the thread is older, what formatting appeared, and whether raw response-control text was shown.

notices.summary: OAuth-gated apps can show a rough logged-out screen.
notices.impact: When someone opens an app that requires OAuth while logged out, the gated screen may look unfinished instead of showing a polished sign-in or access prompt.
notices.workaround: Log in to the right Motion/Runneth account, connect the required OAuth account if needed, then reopen or refresh the app link.

resolution.label: In progress
resolution.note: The logged-out OAuth gate UI is being worked on, but it is not necessarily tied to the next planned release.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Show under Apps. This is a logged-out OAuth gate UI issue, not a general app outage. Use the in_progress resolution flag and do not imply it is confirmed for the next planned release.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks about or reports an app, app link, dashboard, widget, or generated page looking broken, ugly, unfinished, or confusing while logged out or blocked by OAuth.
notices.runnethGuidance: Acknowledge that OAuth-gated apps can show a rough logged-out screen right now, and that the team is working on the UI. Do not imply the authenticated app experience or underlying data is broken unless the user reports that after logging in. Ask the person to log in, open the link from an authenticated Runneth or Motion session, connect the required OAuth account if needed, and refresh the app.
notices.supportGuidance: Capture the app link, whether the person was logged out, which OAuth gate appeared, and whether the page still looks wrong after logging in and refreshing.
